# Kammūpacayakathā (Kv 15.11)

**ID:** Kv 15.11  
**Section:** Kathāvatthu (kv)  
**Collection:** Abhidhamma  
**Title (Pali):** Kammūpacayakathā  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh03m3.mul22.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh03m3.mul22.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kammūpacayakathā* (Kv 15.11) is a debate located in the fifteenth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, the fifth book of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. The discussion centers on whether intentional action (*kamma*) and the accumulation of action (*kammūpacaya*) are distinct phenomena [Park 2007]. According to the commentary (*Kathāvatthuppakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā*), the position distinguishing the two was maintained by the Andhakas and the Sammitīyas [Walser 2005; Park 2007]. They posited that karmic accumulation persists independently of volition, being dissociated from consciousness (*cittavippayutta*), karmically indeterminate (*abyākata*), and without an intentional object (*anārammaṇa*) [Nyanatiloka 2007; Walser 2005]. This model was formulated to explain the mechanism of karmic fruition (*vipāka*) across intervals of time without requiring karmic potential to intrude constantly into ongoing conscious processes [Waldron 2003; Park 2007]. The Theravādin interlocutor refutes this distinction, arguing that karma and its fruition cannot be severed from mental concomitants [Devdas 2004].
